analysis: The code snippet calls `substring` twice: `msg.substring(START_OF_COMMAND_INDEX)` (one-param) when `end == -1`, and `message.substring(START_OF_COMMAND_INDEX, end)` (two-param) otherwise. The provided javadoc only describes the one-param version, throwing IndexOutOfBoundsException if `beginIndex` is negative or larger than the string length. For the two-param version, standard Java behavior throws IndexOutOfBoundsException if `beginIndex` is negative, if `endIndex` is larger than the string length, or if `beginIndex > endIndex`. The code does not validate `START_OF_COMMAND_INDEX`; its value is unknown. In the first branch, if `START_OF_COMMAND_INDEX` is negative or > `msg.length()`, exception occurs. In the second branch, `end` comes from `indexOf(' ')` and is non-negative and < message.length() if a space exists, but `START_OF_COMMAND_INDEX` could be negative or greater than `end`, causing exception. Thus, the throwing condition for IndexOutOfBoundsException is not avoided by any checks.
remark: The exception IndexOutOfBoundsException can be triggered in two scenarios: (1) In the one-param call `msg.substring(START_OF_COMMAND_INDEX)` when `end == -1`, if `START_OF_COMMAND_INDEX` is negative or exceeds `msg.length()`. (2) In the two-param call `message.substring(START_OF_COMMAND_INDEX, end)` when a space exists, if `START_OF_COMMAND_INDEX` is negative or greater than `end` (note that `end` is always less than `message.length()` due to `indexOf` returning a valid index when a space exists). The code lacks any validation of `START_OF_COMMAND_INDEX` against the string length or `end`, so these conditions remain possible.
